paragraphs.text: A [white tea](white:definition) cake from [Fuding](fuding:where-it-is), the coastal city in the far northeast of Fujian, closed in by mountains on three sides with the East China Sea to the east. The leaf was only withered and dried. It was never heated to stop its change and never rolled, so it keeps its natural shape and the white down on its buds. The cake carries the year 2009. That is the same year the area's white tea became a [protected origin name](fuding:on-a-label) in China. The name says where the leaf grew and was made, and nothing about its grade or how long it has aged.

At seventeen years it is well past the seventh year of the [trade saying](fujian-white:ageing) that calls white tea tea in its first year, medicine at three and a treasure at seven. The saying is not a tested claim, and no agreed count of years makes a white tea aged.

White tea was first pressed into [cakes](fujian-white:cakes) in the 2000s, and the practice spread around 2010 because a cake is smaller and easier to keep and carry than loose leaf. That makes this cake one of the early ones. Some cakes were pressed from leaf that had already aged loose for a few years, so 2009 may be the year it was pressed rather than the year it was picked.

brewing.text: Gongfu style, use about 1 gram of leaf to 15 to 25 ml of water, for example 5 grams in a 100 to 110 ml gaiwan; weigh it, since the leaf is light and bulky. Silver Needle and young, delicate tea take water below the boil, about 75 to 90°C; older, leafier or aged tea takes water at or near the boil. Start with a steep of 10 to 45 seconds and add a few seconds each round. An aged cake is often rinsed quickly first, and older pressed tea can be simmered on the stove, about 5 grams to 500 ml for 3 to 10 minutes; young, delicate tea is not.

notice.text: Jujube or dried dates, herbs and medicine, wood, honey and dried fruit, a deeper, redder liquor, a thicker, rounder body, and less lift in the scent than a young tea.

unsupported.sentence: It was never heated to stop its change and never rolled, so it keeps its natural shape and the white down on its buds.
unsupported.words: so it keeps its natural shape and the white down on its buds
unsupported.why: This is a pressed cake, so the leaf does not keep its natural shape. The record gives no grade, and a cake may be Shou Mei, which has few or no buds. So the claim that this lot keeps its shape and the down on its buds is not supported.

unsupported.sentence: That makes this cake one of the early ones.
unsupported.words: That makes this cake one of the early ones
unsupported.why: The cakes claim says the year on a cake may be the year it was picked rather than pressed, and the next sentence says the same. If 2009 is the picking year, the cake may have been pressed later, so the inputs do not show it was one of the early cakes.
